A modern software-engineering agent must successively understand the task specifi-
cation, retrieve the relevant context from a repository, and construct a change that
can then be checked by tests or static analysis. In practice, these functions are often
distributed across several roles: one role builds a plan, another proposes a solution, a
third critiques the intermediate result, and a fourth runs external verification. This
decomposition is conceptually convenient, but it becomes expensive when all roles are
forced to reread the same long context.
